NEXUS ENTERPRISE IT & CYBERSECURITY POLICY

Document Classification: Internal | Revision: 3.2 | Effective Date: January 1, 2026

1. Purpose and Scope

This policy defines mandatory requirements for safeguarding NEXUS enterprise assets, cloud infrastructure, endpoint devices, customer data, and intellectual property. All full-time employees, contractors, and third-party vendors are strictly required to comply.

2. Access Control and Authentication

1.content:
tors, and third-party vendors are strictly required to comply.

2. Access Control and Authentication

All employee accounts must enforce Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA) using hardware security keys or authenticator apps. SMS-based verification is strictly prohibited. Passwords must be at least 14 characters in length and contain uppercase, lowercase, numbers, and symbols. Passwords must not be reused across enterprise and personal services. Session timeouts are enforced after 30 minutes of inactivity on all internal workstations and portals.

2.content:
ssion timeouts are enforced after 30 minutes of inactivity on all internal workstations and portals.

3. Endpoint Security and Disk Encryption

3.content:
es of inactivity on all internal workstations and portals.

3. Endpoint Security and Disk Encryption

All corporate laptops (MacBook, Windows, Linux) must have full-disk encryption enabled (FileVault on macOS, BitLocker on Windows). Installation of unauthorized third-party software, peer-to-peer file sharing clients, or unapproved VPN software is prohibited. Security patches must be applied within 72 hours of critical Common Vulnerabilities and Exposures (CVE) disclosure.

4.content:
s must be applied within 72 hours of critical Common Vulnerabilities and Exposures (CVE) disclosure.

4. Incident Response and Breach Notification

Any suspected security incident, lost laptop, phishing email, or credential compromise must be reported immediately to security@nexus.ai or via the Slack channel #security-alerts within 60 minutes. Failure to report security anomalies may lead to disciplinary action up to contract termination.

5.content:
NEXUS ENTERPRISE REMOTE WORK & WORK FROM HOME POLICY

1. Overview
NEXUS AI recognizes flexible working arrangements to enhance work-life balance and operational efficiency. This policy applies to all full-time salaried staff who have completed their initial 90-day onboarding period.

6.content:
y applies to all full-time salaried staff who have completed their initial 90-day onboarding period.

2. Core Collaboration Hours
To facilitate cross-functional teamwork across global time zones, all remote team members are expected to be available for synchronous communication on Slack, email, and Google Meet between 10:00 AM and 4:00 PM in their designated primary regional time zone.

7.content:
email, and Google Meet between 10:00 AM and 4:00 PM in their designated primary regional time zone.

3. Home Office Setup & Equipment Stipend
Full-time remote employees receive a one-time home office reimbursement of $1,500 for ergonomic chairs, standing desks, high-resolution monitors, and noise-canceling headsets. An ongoing monthly internet stipend of $80 is processed automatically with payroll.

8.content:
celing headsets. An ongoing monthly internet stipend of $80 is processed automatically with payroll.

4. Confidentiality & Physical Security in Remote Environments
When working from home, co-working spaces, or public locations, employees must ensure that computer screens are not visible to unauthorized persons. Using public, unencrypted Wi-Fi networks without activating the corporate WireGuard/Tailscale VPN is prohibited. Printing sensitive customer or financial data at home is strictly forbidden.

9.content:
cale VPN is prohibited. Printing sensitive customer or financial data at home is strictly forbidden.

5. Time Tracking & Performance Measurement
Remote employees are evaluated based on sprint deliverables, objectives and key results (OKRs), and code/document output rather than continuous desk hours. Sick days and personal leaves must be logged through the HR portal at least 24 hours in advance, except in medical emergencies.

NEXUS AGILE PROJECT MANAGEMENT FRAMEWORK

Engineering & Operations SOP | Version 2.4 | Owner: PMO Office

1. Sprint Cadence and Planning Cycles

All engineering, product, and AI research squads operate on two-week sprint cycles beginning on Wednesdays. Sprint Planning occurs bi-weekly on Wednesday at 10:00 AM, backlog grooming every second Monday, and Sprint Retrospectives on alternate Tuesdays at 4:00 PM.

2. Definition of Done (DoD)

18.content:
ond Monday, and Sprint Retrospectives on alternate Tuesdays at 4:00 PM.

2. Definition of Done (DoD)

A feature or ticket is classified as Done only when: (1) All acceptance criteria are satisfied, (2) Unit and integration test coverage is at or above 80%, (3) Static analysis and security scanning (SonarQube/Snyk) pass with zero critical vulnerabilities, (4) Peer review is approved by at least two senior engineers, (5) Technical documentation and API contracts in Swagger/Postman are updated.

19.content:
two senior engineers, (5) Technical documentation and API contracts in Swagger/Postman are updated.

3. Incident Escalation & Post-Mortem Standards

Sev-1 and Sev-2 incidents trigger PagerDuty alerts to on-call squads within 5 minutes. A blameless post-mortem document must be authored within 48 hours of resolution, detailing timeline, root cause analysis (5 Whys), preventative action items, and Jira tracking tickets.

20.content:
NEXUS ENTERPRISE GLOBAL DATA PRIVACY & COMPLIANCE POLICY

1. Legal & Regulatory Compliance
NEXUS AI is committed to maintaining compliance with the General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR), the California Consumer Privacy Act (CCPA), and SOC 2 Type II criteria.

21.content:
rotection Regulation (GDPR), the California Consumer Privacy Act (CCPA), and SOC 2 Type II criteria.

2. Personally Identifiable Information (PII) Classification
PII includes names, email addresses, phone numbers, IP addresses, financial account numbers, and biometric records. All PII collected during user interactions, search sessions, and enterprise document ingestion must be tokenized or pseudonymized before persistence.

22.content:
h sessions, and enterprise document ingestion must be tokenized or pseudonymized before persistence.

3. Encryption & Data Protection Standards
All data in transit must be secured with TLS 1.3 cryptographic protocols. All customer databases, vector storage files, and document blobs must be encrypted at rest using AES-256 encryption. Encryption keys are rotated every 90 days via AWS KMS or HashiCorp Vault.

23.content:
using AES-256 encryption. Encryption keys are rotated every 90 days via AWS KMS or HashiCorp Vault.

4. Right to Erasure & Data Subject Access Requests (DSAR)
Customers and enterprise employees have the right to request access to or permanent deletion of their indexed documents and search history. DSAR requests must be fulfilled by the Compliance Team within 30 calendar days of verification.

24.content:
ory. DSAR requests must be fulfilled by the Compliance Team within 30 calendar days of verification.

5. Data Retention & Destruction
Search query logs and telemetry are retained for 365 days for machine learning performance optimization and security auditing, after which they are automatically purged. When enterprise contracts terminate, tenant vector indexes and document stores are securely wiped within 14 days using DoD 5220.22-M sanitization standards.

Engineers branch from 'main' using convention 'feat/TICKET-description' or 'fix/TICKET-description'. Direct commits to 'main' or 'staging' branches are locked and restricted by branch protection rules. Pull requests require green CI pipeline status, automated linting passing, and 2 approvals. 2.
